newsitem.title: PERU: Japanese ambassador's residence in Peru attacked.
newsitem.headline: Japanese ambassador's residence in Peru attacked.

text.p: Up to 40 armed attackers overran the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima on Tuesday and held up 40 hostages, Peruvian officials and eyewitnesses said.
"There has been an attack against the residence of the Japanese ambassador," said Peruvian Health Minister Marino Costa Bauer on local radio.
The attack took place during a reception attended by senior government officials and other dignataries.

From a nearby roof a Reuters photographer saw an estimated 40 hostages inside and up to 20 attackers armed with guns and hand grenades. Witnesses said they presumed the attack was by one of Peru's two communist guerrilla groups, the Maoist Shining Path or the smaller Cuban-inspired Tupac Amaru Revolutioanry Movement (MRTA).

No officials could confirm these versions. Police said shots were from the residency at 8 p.m. EST (0100 GMT Wednesday) but it was not clear at what time the incident began. The firing had died down within two hours.
